questions.explain: Contact forces need touch. Magnetic, electrostatic and gravitational forces act across a gap.

questions.prompt: Two magnets are placed with their north poles facing each other. They will…
questions.explain: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

questions.prompt: Which object will a magnet NOT attract?

feedback.2: Correct: aluminium is a metal, but it isn’t magnetic.

questions.explain: Only a few metals (iron, nickel, cobalt, and steel which contains iron) are magnetic.

questions.prompt: Match each force to an example.

pairs.right: A balloon sticking to a wall

questions.explain: Every force has an everyday example.

questions.prompt: A balloon rubbed on hair sticks to the wall. Which force holds it there?
questions.explain: Rubbing transfers electric charge, and the charged balloon attracts the wall: an electrostatic force.

questions.prompt: A pin is placed at different distances from a magnet. Order from STRONGEST pull to WEAKEST.
questions.explain: Non-contact forces get weaker as the gap increases.
N–N and S–S repel; N–S attract.

questions.prompt: Adam measured how many paper clips a magnet could hold at different gaps: 0 cm → 12 clips, 1 cm → 7, 2 cm → 3, 3 cm → 1. Describe the pattern and explain it.
questions.modelAnswer: As the gap increases, the number of paper clips held decreases, from 12 at 0 cm to 1 at 3 cm. This shows the magnetic force gets weaker with distance. The force falls quickly at first and then more slowly.
rubric: Describes the trend: larger gap, fewer clips
Concludes that magnetic force weakens with distance
questions.explain: Criterion C: describe the trend using the data, then explain it scientifically.

questions.prompt: Which statement about gravity is true?
options: It acts between all objects that have mass
It only pulls on heavy objects
questions.explain: Every mass attracts every other mass. The Moon, Sun and planets all have gravity.
